rules.evidence: Lake Powell's 'nearly ran dry' premise flipped: from the 3,516.62 ft record low (Sept 15, 2026) the lake rose to 3,538.11 ft by Nov 6 (+21.5 ft) and the feed turned to 'RISING'. The Karl Bushby news peak (2 Nov) would have faded before a quality film shipped (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json finalists[lake-powell-drained].red, curated.dropped).

rules.rule: Do not choose or open with subjects where humour is off-limits and taste is risky (living residents of a tragedy, child deaths), and never put a flippant line next to a tragedy.

The 1946 Laupahoehoe cold open (16 schoolchildren killed) was cut because 'We're going to finish the job' over child deaths is glib and clashes with the owner's funny-scenes brief (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json curated.dropped, finalists[hawaii-without-ocean].red kill shot 5; brief.md section 4 must-fix 5).

rules.rule: Never make a fact that mega-view Shorts or long-forms have already spent the climax. Search the climax claim with ytsearch.py, use the least-claimed true number as the payoff at 85-90% of runtime, and keep the worn fact as a mid-film beat.
rules.evidence: 'Mauna Kea is taller than Everest' is spent (Shorts at 17M, 2.1M and 376K; Be Smart 3.64M). Mauna Loa at about 56,000 ft from its depressed base (USGS) had only a 38K and a 1.4K video near it, so it became the payoff and the Everest fact moved to 3:55 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json finalists[hawaii-without-ocean].red kill shot 2, fix 3; brief.md sections 3, 7).

rules.rule: Never ship a thumbnail with more than one graphic device, more than 3 words or a navy/dark-dominated background. One focal subject fills at least 50% of the frame, at least 40% of the area is bright or saturated, and each text line is at least 20% of the thumbnail height, white on a black box with one accent-colour word.
rules.evidence: Ep01's thumbnail had about 5 competing elements (3 orange continents, 3 arrows, a ring, a '?' and 3 words) on a dark navy map; overall CTR 2.27%, Suggested 1.97% (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons P5; context.md). The breakout thumbnails (RealLifeLore zkbgLhBmzGo, Antarctica TudM_lSW8WA, Zanclean Mg0DMsmg9WM) all use one tilted, close terrain view (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.bench finding 1).

rules.rule: Before upload, mock every thumbnail in dark mode at 390x220 pt (phone card) and 168x94 px (compact card) next to the 5 strongest host thumbnails; if ours is not the brightest and most readable card in the strip, redo it or default to the no-text variant.
rules.evidence: 93% of ep01's impressions were Suggested, at 1.97% CTR (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/context.md). The ep02 brief makes this test mandatory and names the no-text Thumbnail 2 as the fallback if 'SEA LEVEL' is unreadable at 168x94 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md section 5; topic_hunt.json lessons P1).

rules.rule: Never use a title over 50 characters or with hedge words ('Not Just', 'Sort Of', 'Maybe', 'Kind Of'). Write 35-50 characters, with the proper noun in the first 3 words and one concrete noun the viewer can picture.
rules.evidence: Ep01: 'Why the Continents Point South (Not Just a Coincidence)', 55 characters with the bracket spent on a hedge; CTR 2.27%. The niche outlier median is 51 characters, and compact cards cut titles past about 45 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons P2). Ep02 launch title: 'Hawaii Is Only the Tip. We Drained the Ocean.' (45) (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md section 5).

rules.rule: Never build the curiosity gap on an abstract question the viewer did not have before seeing the card; withhold one specific, concrete thing they already want to know (what is at the bottom, the tip of what, why nobody may land there).
rules.evidence: Ep01's thumbnail text 'POINTING AT WHAT?' asked viewers to care about a pattern first; Suggested CTR was 1.97% (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons P4; ep01 thumbnail /home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep01-continental-drip/release/thumb_B_pointing_at_what.jpg, cited in lessons.topic_vs_execution).

rules.rule: Never launch with a title that copies an incumbent's exact words or a template that clone channels are farming. Reuse the host cluster's key nouns (e.g. 'Drained', 'Ocean') in our own sentence, name the subject in the first spoken sentence and the first description line, and keep exact search phrases in the description and tags.
rules.evidence: 'What Hawaii Looks Like Without Water' is owned by a 105-minute, 9.0K-view sleep doc. 'We Drained X. Here's What Was Hidden at the Bottom.' was cloned lake by lake within days (Contour Atlas, The Hidden Provinces), with views dropping on each copy; using it means we 'land as a late clone' (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json finalists[hawaii-without-ocean].red kill shot 8, finalists[lake-powell-drained].red, lessons P3; brief.md section 4 must-fix 6, section 5).

rules.rule: Make the thumbnail an honest, stronger render of a real shot from the film, showing the BEFORE or partial state of the hero reveal. Use that exact composition as frame 1 in motion, pay off part of the promise within 30 s (the title by about 0:10), and return to the same camera, subject and accent colour for the payoff.
rules.evidence: The breakout drain videos' thumbnails are stronger versions of shots in their films (Contour Atlas' -351 FT basin, the drained Mediterranean slab, Antarctica's ice lid); ep01 had no such frame (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.bench finding 'Design the main visual so a frame from the film can be the thumbnail'). Frame 1 = thumbnail was kept from ep01 (topic_hunt.json lessons P6, P7, V7; brief.md section 6).

rules.rule: Test 3 thumbnails in Test & Compare (with the owner's OK) and judge nothing before about 10K impressions. Judge on Suggested CTR (target 5%+) and watch time per impression = CTR x average view duration (ep01 5.2 s, target 15 s+). Change one variable at a time and never the title and thumbnail on the same day.
rules.evidence: At ep01's 925 impressions, a 2% vs 3% difference is noise; ep01's watch time per impression = 2.27% x 231 s = 5.2 s (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons P8, P9). The brief's stall rule: if impressions stall below about 3K after 72 h, make one change, then wait 72 h (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md section 5).

rules.rule: Never open with a menu or table of contents ('along the way', 'by the end you'll know', a list of upcoming topics); allow at most one forward promise, and it must be the story's own question.
rules.evidence: YouTube's retention critique of ep01: the intro stacked a table of contents at 0:37-0:54 ('dig to China, 1875 theory, future collisions') (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/context.md; topic_hunt.json lessons H6).

rules.rule: Put no historical asides, quotes, Latin, static portraits, book pages or idea-history dates in the first 2 minutes.
rules.evidence: YouTube flagged ep01's Bacon Latin quote over a static portrait (1:00-1:25) as too slow (context.md). The frame audit measured about 50 s of static paper and portraits at 0:57-1:16 and 1:40-2:12, about 44% of the first 131 s, exactly where phone viewers left at 2:11 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 3).

rules.rule: Never hold back the first hero shot past 0:30. Show the best photoreal reveal (with part of the thumbnail payoff) by 0:14-0:30, then a new hero shot about every 1.5-2 minutes.
rules.evidence: Ep01's best shot, the antipode overlay, came at 2:40, after the average phone viewer had already left at 2:11 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons H4, V4; context.md). Ep02 plans its hero shots at 0:00 and 0:14 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md sections 6, 11).

rules.rule: In 0:00-1:00 use at most 2 named people, 1 date and 1 number, and keep every sentence to 15 words or fewer (12 or fewer in the first 30 s).
rules.evidence: Ep01's first chapter (0:00-2:15) packed about 5 named people or sources, 5 dates or eras, 2 statistics and a 3-item menu; phone viewers averaged 2:11 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons H8). The ep02 cold open is 71 words with 0 names, 0 dates and 1 number (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md section 6).

rules.rule: Never open on a slow whole-globe drift or a small globe in black. Open close, at regional zoom, with something moving every second and a new visual event every 2-3 s in minute 1.
rules.evidence: 79.4% of ep01's frames in the first 131 s were at least 45% near-black; on a phone the opening globe was a ~190 px disc inside 390 px of black (0:00, 0:20, 0:40) (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 1; topic_hunt.json lessons H10).

rules.rule: Make frame 1 the thumbnail in motion, with no logo, title card or intro sting. The first spoken line names the subject and the stakes in 12 words or fewer, and the central question is stated in the title's own words by 0:15. The first 10 s must read with the sound off (motion plus ONE big label); upload accurate captions instead of burning in full subtitles.
rules.evidence: Contour Atlas's hook shows a drain-plug gag at 0:01 and its best moving shots in the first 33 s under one story question (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.bench finding 'Cutting rhythm'). None of the long-form winners checked burn in full subtitles (diag.bench keep). Home-feed inline playback starts muted, and Suggested autoplay viewers never chose the video (topic_hunt.json lessons H1-H3).

rules.rule: Never put a subscribe, like, comment or 'Juice Check / Subscribe' ask or graphic inside the story; show no call-to-action graphic before the last 20 s, and use the Juice Check stamp only for verdicts.
rules.evidence: YouTube's critique: ep01's 'Juice Check / Subscribe' break at 4:57-5:07 broke the flow right before the strongest reveal (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/context.md). The audit shows a red SUBSCRIBE pill landing over the tetrahedron reveal at 5:00-5:07 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 9; topic_hunt.json lessons C10).

rules.rule: Never answer the core question before about 85% of the runtime, and never add a recap, extra sections or a speculative coda after the answer; the full answer lands at 85-90% as the last story beat.
rules.evidence: Ep01 answered at 9:13-10:43 (59-69% of runtime), then ran about 4:50 of extra sections (the joke, what doesn't drip, future supercontinents). YouTube: end the moment the last line lands (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons C9, E1; context.md). The ep02 payoff is planned at 11:10-11:45, 87-91% (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md section 7).

rules.rule: Cut or add a new visual event every 3-5 s (every 2-3 s in minute 1), with an average shot of 4-4.5 s or less. Hold no composition longer than 7 s (a live drain may run 10 s while the level and camera keep moving) and nothing fully static longer than 2 s. Change shot scale every 5-7 s, alternate the subject between the left and right thirds, and fly point to point in 1.5-3 s with easing.
rules.evidence: Ep01's QC flagged 25 near-static stretches over 3.5 s (README count: 10.75 s between hard cuts), and its longest uncut stretch was 32.2 s (5:24.6-5:56.8). The audit's detected cut spacing (5.3 s) was on benchmark, so sameness of scale and centred framing was the core problem (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 11; topic_hunt.json lessons C1, C2). Contour Atlas averages 3.5-4.2 s per shot, with a longest hold of about 6.5 s (diag.bench finding 'Cutting rhythm').

rules.rule: Re-hook every 60-90 s (a reveal, a change of location, an in-world gag or a new open question) and make each chapter top the last in stakes or spectacle. Use 5-6 chapters of 2-3 minutes (chapter 1 at most 1:30), titled with teasers in the story's own words: never 'Intro' or 'Conclusion', and never the answer.
rules.evidence: Ep01 peaked at 2:40, then slid into a history of ideas; it had 9 chapters averaging 1:44, the shortest 63 s (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons C7, C8). The ep02 re-hook map has 17 re-hooks in 12:45 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md section 7).

rules.rule: Write narration for 150-160 wpm with sentences of 15 words or fewer, at most 2 new ideas and 1 spoken number per minute, every idea shown on screen, and quotes under 10 words used only when the picture shows the action.
rules.evidence: Ep01's density (5 names, 5 dates and 2 statistics in chapter 1) went with a 2:11 phone average (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons H8, C5, C6). The ep02 budget is about 1,930 words at 153 wpm for 12:45-13:00 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md section 7).

rules.rule: Use about 6-10 big vivid numbers per long-form, each landing on the spoken word as a rolling counter in Anton at 150-190 px cap height (14-18% of frame height). This owner rule overrides the older caps (5 in the lessons, 4 in the ep02 brief).
rules.evidence: Owner standing rule (newest wins). Older plans: 'at most 5 big on-screen numbers' (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons C5) and '4 big on-screen numbers' (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md section 7). Counter size from the look book (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual/visual_plan.md section 2).

rules.rule: Never explain an abstract mechanism (hotspot, flexure, plate motion) for more than about 20 s, and always explain it as one physical metaphor in motion ('a bowling ball on a mattress', 'a sheet of paper over a candle') with no jargon on screen.
rules.evidence: Red team: the Moho/flexure cut-away, hotspot mechanics and Emperor bend are 'the same abstract geology that lost ep01's phone viewers (2:11 average on mobile)' (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json finalists[hawaii-without-ocean].red kill shot 7, fix 8; brief.md Ch4 5:45-6:05 and Ch6 11:10).

rules.rule: Plan a second engine for the second half: when the film's repeating reveal (e.g. the drain ladder) bottoms out mid-film, switch to a new device with its own counter (e.g. a '+ million years' time machine along the island chain) instead of a flyover of similar-looking places.
rules.evidence: Red team kill shot 1: the drain ladder bottoms out at about -5,500 m halfway through, and the second half turns into a sideways flyover of small, similar NW islands, the 'weak middle' where phone viewers leave. Fix 2 splits the film into a drain half and a time-machine half (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json finalists[hawaii-without-ocean].red).

rules.rule: Target 12:30-14:00 (aim for 13:00, about 1,950-2,100 words) with a hard ceiling of 15:00 and no tail after the payoff; a story-heavy film may run longer only if every extra minute carries its own hero shot.
rules.evidence: Ep01 ran 15:34, needed 77 s cut in post and carried about 4:50 after its answer. Yet desktop (7:53, 50.7%) and TV (8:24, 54.1%) viewers stayed for half the film, so length was not what drove phone viewers away. Spectacle outliers win at 11-12 min (Antarctica 11:21) (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/topic_hunt.json lessons.target_length; context.md).

rules.rule: Build the whole film as one visual world: photoreal Earth stages (globe, DEM terrain and seafloor, paper cut-outs on the map) rendered as WORLD, then one shared POST pass (one grade), then a crisp UI layer drawn after post, with one font system, one accent system and one label style. No separate stylised sets.
rules.evidence: YouTube criticised ep01's stylised corridor (7:35-7:50) for clashing with the photoreal globe (context.md). The frame audit counted at least 12 visual languages in 15 minutes (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 4). The panel said the prototypes' different grades and fonts would 'look like two different films', and overlays sent through bloom/DOF lost the crisp edges that made the antipode shot work (visual_upgrade.json panel drain, globe; /home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual/visual_plan.md section 1.1, U1).

rules.rule: Never use a small centred globe on black as the default shot. Make tilted full-bleed oblique and terrain shots at least 60% of runtime; keep whole-globe-in-space shots to at most 10% of runtime and 4 s each, filling the frame height when used; and on globes that carry a map fact, keep clouds at 0-0.35 and off the subject.
rules.evidence: 74.0% of ep01's frames were at least 45% near-black and only 7.1% were full-bleed; on a phone the globe was a ~190 px disc in 390 px of black. Ep01's full-bleed tilted shots (7:50, 12:20, 12:40, 15:08) read perfectly at 390 px (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 1). Panel: the CineGlobe Atlantic story globe at clouds 0.62 read worse than ep01 on a phone, with Florida a 6-8 px smear (visual_upgrade.json panel globe).

rules.rule: Keep every oblique, terrain and story shot at a mean luma of 70/255 or more, the whole film at 85-130, near-black pixels (luma under 18) at 15% or less, and no run over 4 s below luma 40. Show no night-side globe unless the city lights are the point; mood comes from light and weather, never from black frames.
rules.evidence: Ep01's mean luma was about 40 (per-minute means 17.7-67.7), with 50 s continuously below 28 at 13:27-14:17. Benchmarks: Contour Atlas 161, RealLifeLore 166, Ice Melt 118, Wendover 105 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 6, diag.bench finding 1; visual/visual_plan.md section 2).

rules.rule: Draw hero highlights in the praised antipode style: one hero shape per frame, a 55-66% fill so the relief shows through, a crisp 5-6 px white outline and a soft glow, with the surroundings dimmed and desaturated. Never use a 100% opaque fill.
rules.evidence: YouTube called ep01's antipode overlay (2:40-3:05) 'remarkably vivid and professional', and it still reads at 390 px (context.md; visual_upgrade.json diag.audit keep). The story prototype's 100% fills hid the relief, and the type prototype's 66% salmon fill hid the very overlap it claimed (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json panel story, type; visual/visual_plan.md section 9).

rules.rule: Show change live on one fixed camera (drain, flood, ice peel, time slider) for 4-10 s while the gauge ticks and a riser or rumble plays; never show a change as a cut between two states.
rules.evidence: Contour Atlas drops its water planes live, with a 'WATER LEVEL' widget counting -3 FT to -351 FT (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.bench findings 3-4). Our live drain prototype took the teen-on-phone score from 3 to 8: 'the most scroll-stopping thing in all four prototypes' (visual_upgrade.json panel drain).

rules.rule: Never render terrain at 3x vertical exaggeration or more. Use 1.0 in every shot that compares heights and at most 1.5-2x elsewhere, never mix values within a shot, and say 'heights exaggerated' once in the narration whenever it is above 1.0.
rules.evidence: Panel on the drain prototype: 3x relief looked like 'spiky crumpled foil' and '2005 game terrain' (TV viewer 5 to 7, motion director 4 to 6). The tech scout's 6x made the mountains spiky (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json panel drain, diag.tech finding 2; visual/visual_plan.md section 9; brief.md section 8).

rules.rule: Never put characters in gradient voids, separate stylised sets, Kenney block-kid scenes or flat-vector interiors, or at about 10% of frame height. Every character stands on the real terrain at 35-40% of frame height or more, lit by the same sun, with a soft contact shadow and the shared grade.
rules.evidence: YouTube criticised ep01's stylised corridor (7:35-7:50). The audit found a faceted adventurer in a blue/purple void with two disagreeing shadows (7:37-7:43), a character at about 10% of frame height, about 20 px on a phone (5:25-5:53), and block kids with placeholder chalk lines (6:20) (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 5; context.md).

rules.rule: Whatever the narration names must fill at least a third of the frame width (aim for 50-70% of frame height), and every highlighted shape must be at least 25 px wide on a 390 px phone frame (about 120 px at 1080p); if not, move the camera closer or add an inset zoom.
rules.evidence: On a phone, ep01's Florida highlight was 6-8 px and Greenland, Baja, Kamchatka and India were a few mm wide (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual/visual_plan.md section 2; topic_hunt.json lessons T8, C4). The ep02 brief uses inset zooms because a 250 m ship on a 300 km frame is invisible (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/brief.md section 8).

rules.rule: Never draw a meaningful line thinner than 6 px at 1080p. Lines get a 9-12 px core with a dark under-stroke 8 px wider plus glow; arrows a 15 px body and a 50-63 px head; outlines 5-6 px; pins a radius of 11 px or more. Every line draws on with a moving head dot.
rules.evidence: Ep01's meaningful strokes were 3-5 px at 1080p, about 1 px on a phone (0:05 great-circle arc, 3:40 equator, 13:30-14:00 drift arrows) (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 12; visual/visual_plan.md section 2).

rules.rule: Never show mock documents, fake papers with grey dash 'text' bars or placeholder graphics; show a real public-domain scan cropped to 5 big words or fewer, or tell the moment on the map.
rules.evidence: Ep01 showed grey-dash mock papers (1:51-2:09, 11:40) and a '1976' mock paper titled 'THE DRIP, REVISITED' that looks like a real publication, which risks breaking the owner's no-false-claims rule (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 8).

rules.rule: Show public-domain archival stills full-bleed and always moving (Ken Burns 1.5-3% per 10 s) with the shared grade: at most 3 s per still, 5 s per clip and 1 per minute, never two in a row in the first 3 minutes, and never a static portrait under an aside.
rules.evidence: Kept from ep01: the 1930 Greenland photo filling the frame at 8:20 was authentic and emotional. Rejected: static portraits and book pages at 0:57-1:16 and 1:40-2:12 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit keep, finding 3; topic_hunt.json lessons V3; visual/visual_plan.md section 4 S12).

rules.rule: Never use grids, thumbnail mosaics, 4-way split screens, overlapping pins, ghosted texture backgrounds or colour legends. State colour meaning with coloured headline words, and show lists as full-frame tilted shots joined by whip-pans (1-1.5 s per quick item, 4-7 s per explained item).
rules.evidence: Ep01 at 12:00 showed 8 thumbnails at about 36x24 px on a phone; the 3:12 legend (about 3 px on a phone) carried the meaning of 4:00-4:40; 0:54 was a 4-way split of near-black globes; pins overlapped at 11:00-11:20 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit findings 6, 10).

rules.rule: Give each film one persistent gauge for its one changing variable (sea level, depth, year) in a fixed corner at 12-15% of frame height, in the same position in every mode for the whole chapter, with ticks while it moves and an impact cue on milestones.
rules.evidence: Contour Atlas keeps its 'WATER LEVEL' widget in the same corner across terrain, diorama and photo shots (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.bench finding 3). Ep01's million-years counter was small and appeared in only one sequence (9:23-10:23). The drain prototype's giant SEA LEVEL gauge was the panel teen's top pick (visual_upgrade.json panel drain).

rules.rule: Never ship a frame with a camera-sun specular smudge, additive blob sprites, blurred dark smears used as text plates, rectangle-clipped fills, text over text, texture seams or hairlines.
rules.evidence: Ep01 had a grey specular smudge beside South America at 0:00 (the very first frame), Antarctica as a white blob with bubbly cloud sprites at 1:18-1:24, a dark smear behind the '115' counter at 10:00, fills cut by rectangle edges at 12:00 and a headline over page text at 5:08 (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 7). The prototypes still had an Antilles swath seam and a shelf hairline (visual_upgrade.json panel globe).

rules.rule: Set must-read text (place labels, name plates, gauge titles) at a cap height of 64 px or more at 1080p (5.9% of frame height, about 13 px on a phone), nothing anywhere below a 48 px cap, and headlines in Anton at a 96-120 px cap with at most 4 words.
rules.evidence: Ep01's labels and captions had a 26-35 px cap (2.5-3% of height), which is 5-7 px on a phone; e.g. 0:25 'NEARLY 9 IN 10 OF US' at about 6 px (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.audit finding 2). The type prototype using this floor took the panel teen from 2 to 8 ('every word reads at 390 px'); verdict ADOPT (visual_upgrade.json panel type; visual/visual_plan.md sections 2, 9).

rules.rule: Never use grey on-screen text, 'SIMPLIFIED'-style sub-lines, pill-shaped labels, Bebas or near-transparent plates. Use Anton for headlines and numbers, Barlow Condensed 800 caps for labels, and #F4F6FA text on a rectangular rgba(6,9,15,0.86) plate with an 8 px accent bar; on bright terrain or sky always use a plate, not just a scrim.

The look book retired Bebas and pills because Anton survives the 0.2x downscale and the re-encode, and the panel demanded one system. This supersedes the brief's 'white text in a black pill' (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual/visual_plan.md sections 1.2, 1.3, 9; brief.md section 8).

rules.rule: Never drop a qualifier ('MOST OF', 'NEARLY', 'ABOUT', 'FROM ITS TRUE BASE') to fit a word cap; put it in a kicker of up to 2 words, or show the share as a number.
rules.evidence: The type prototype's headline 'ANTARCTICA IS OPPOSITE THE ARCTIC OCEAN' dropped 'MOST OF' and overclaimed; the panel made it blocker B1 under the no-false-claims rule (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual/visual_plan.md section 8; visual_upgrade.json panel type).

rules.rule: Show at most one text block plus one map label plus the gauge (10 visible words at most). Keep must-read text in the top 62% of the frame (above y=670 at 1080p), out of the top 8% and inside a 5% safe margin, in the third opposite the subject, and rotate 3-4 layouts rather than using one template.
rules.evidence: Phone player controls and captions cover the bottom of the frame (/home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual_upgrade.json diag.tech finding 1; topic_hunt.json lessons C3). The panel found that the same left-third layout in every shot 'becomes a template', leaving 40% of each frame as empty navy (visual_upgrade.json panel type; /home/user/juicytea-media/longform/ep02-hawaii/research/visual/visual_plan.md section 2).

rules.rule: Never show sources, citations, author-year names, data credits or 'computed from data' lines on screen; all credits (e.g. GEBCO, SOEST HMRG, USGS, NOAA photo credits) go in the description only.

Use comic sound effects only on gags, and give every funny script line its own visual.

result.verdict: NOT READY TO COMMIT AS IS. The playbook covers every standing owner rule. The four files contain no secrets, tokens, keys, personal emails or owner names (grep-verified), and no AI wording that could leak into video content. 27 numbers were spot-checked against the sources and 22 match exactly: Studio 925/2.27%/862/1.97%/34 at 8.82%/9 search; device AVDs; US 28%/43%; Hawaii 218 = 77/67/74; hosts 7.07M/3.64M/3.04M; Powell +21.5 ft; Mauna Loa 56,000 ft vs 38K/1.4K videos; 97 defects (1 blocker, 40 major, 18 pops); 7 of 109 false starts; s035 4.82 vs 3.80 (+27%); scratch +5.8 dB; Wegener 6/6; seam ratio 12.4; 38 to 13.7 deg/frame; -14.0 LUFS / LRA 2.3 / TP -1.4; 84 cuts, 10.99 s mean, 84.8 s max; audit 74.0%/7.1%/79.4%/190 px/32.2 s/26-35 px caps; panel teen 2 to 8 and 3 to 8; redteam 8 of 109; 19.3 s of re-reads and the 17.9 s Nevada cut; Lake Peigneur -14.1 LUFS, TP -3.2, 8.00 PASS; San Juan MAE 4.4/255; Bats 23-41 s/frame. The blocking problems: (1) the GitHub repo is PUBLIC, and CLAUDE.md says to push after every task; (2) PLAYBOOK.md is about 31K tokens, so the standard Read tool shows only lines 1-296 and agents never see the Shorts, pipeline, QC, delivery and Superseded sections; (3) the AI-wording grep gate cannot pass on a Hawaii film, because "AI" matches HAWAII and Drained; (4) the ep01 owner was told to upload the ~3.7 Mbps size-capped copy, and the tools hardcode H.264 level 4.2, which is invalid for the planned 1440p upload; (5) several gates are weaker than or contradict the rules they enforce (typeqc, blackdetect, silence, numbers, music beds, legends, globe caps); (6) the competitor-edge guidance the owner is asking about is a single untestable hypothesis bullet.
